evals.name: business-rules-beyond-schema
evals.prompt: I need to work on the approval logic in this repository and don't know the domain yet. Get me oriented to the domain model before I touch anything. The repository is at evals/domain-orientation/cases/case-001/repo/.
evals.expected_output: Identifies Report, Expense, Employee, and Approval as first-class domain concepts, grounds the receipt-required-above-threshold rule and the self-approval/management-chain approval rule in rules.py as observed business invariants (not schema constraints), and treats AuditEvent as an implementation artifact rather than a modeled domain concept.
expectations: Names at least the receipt-required-above-threshold rule and the cannot-self-approve / must-be-in-management-chain rule as observed business invariants grounded in rules.py, not merely restating models.py's field list or NOT NULL-level constraints

AuditEvent is identified as an implementation artifact (a generic append-only log with no invariant or business rule of its own), not given a full first-class domain-concept entry alongside Report/Expense/Employee/Approval

Report's status field is named as carrying its own lifecycle (draft/submitted/approved/rejected with transition guards in rules.py), flagged as a lifecycle-audit candidate rather than a full transition-by-transition characterization being inlined here

evals.name: policy-not-persisted-row
evals.prompt: I need to work in this repository and don't know the domain yet. Get me oriented to the domain model before I touch anything. The repository is at evals/domain-orientation/cases/case-002/repo/.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the promotion gate/policy (soak time, required approvals) as the load-bearing domain concept even though it has no dedicated persisted table -- eligibility is computed fresh from POLICY, Deployment fields, and Approval rows -- rather than only listing Deployment and Approval as the domain model.
expectations: Names the gate/policy concept (a named check a deployment must clear to be eligible to promote) as a first-class domain concept in its own right, grounded in gates/ and promotion.py, not merely described as implementation detail of the Deployment class

States explicitly that promotion eligibility is not a persisted field or row anywhere -- it's computed on demand from POLICY, the deployment's own fields, and Approval rows -- rather than inventing or implying a 'PromotionRequest' or eligibility-status entity that doesn't exist in the evidence
Approval is characterized as an input a gate reads (a vote/precondition), not as something with its own lifecycle or as the entity that decides eligibility

evals.name: terminology-map-same-and-different
evals.prompt: I need to work in this repository and don't know the domain yet. Get me oriented to the domain model before I touch anything. The repository is at evals/domain-orientation/cases/case-003/repo/.
evals.expected_output: Correctly identifies billing.Customer and the API's 'account' as the same underlying concept under two names (grounded in get_account calling get_customer with the same id), and correctly identifies loyalty.Member as a genuinely distinct concept from Customer with different cardinality (one Member can link to multiple Customers via MemberCustomerLink; a Customer may have zero Members), rather than collapsing or conflating either pair.
expectations: A terminology map or equivalent explicitly states that the API's 'account' (account_id, account_email) and billing.Customer are the same underlying concept under two different names, grounded in api/schemas.py's get_account calling billing's get_customer with the same id -- not just noted as coincidentally similar

Member is explicitly identified as NOT the same concept as Customer, grounded in the many-to-many MemberCustomerLink cardinality (one household Member can link to more than one Customer; a Customer can have zero Members) -- not collapsed into Customer/Account just because it's an adjacent-sounding people/identity concept
Authority is stated per concept: billing owns Customer identity, loyalty owns Member -- not one undifferentiated 'user identity' owner across both

evals.name: tooling-domain-not-business
evals.prompt: I need to work in this repository and don't know the domain yet. Get me oriented to the domain model before I touch anything. The repository is at evals/domain-orientation/cases/case-004/repo/.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is a technical/tooling domain (a lease-based job queue), correctly maps Job/Lease/DeadLetterEntry and the fencing-token invariant as the domain concepts, and does not force retail/business vocabulary onto it or conclude there's no domain here because it's infrastructure.
expectations: Domain shape (or equivalent) explicitly characterizes this as a technical/tooling domain (job queue / lease semantics), not a business domain, and does not force business-style vocabulary (customer, order, account) onto it

States the fencing-token invariant as an observed business/domain rule -- a stale completion (mismatched fencing_token) is silently dropped rather than erroring or completing the job -- grounded in leasing.py's complete()

Lease is identified as not independently persisted (it's fields grouped on Job's own storage, per Lease's own docstring and acquire()'s actual store calls) rather than treated as its own separately-stored entity

evals.name: real-bounded-context-boundary
evals.prompt: I need to work in this repository and don't know the domain yet. Get me oriented to the domain model before I touch anything. The repository is at evals/domain-orientation/cases/case-005/repo/.
evals.expected_output: Correctly identifies auth.Account and billing.Account as two genuinely distinct domain concepts that happen to share a name, connected only through the explicit AccountLink translation table in integration/, and does not collapse them into one concept or claim a boundary exists between other parts of the repo without similar evidence.
expectations: States that auth.Account (login identity) and billing.Account (subscription/plan) are two distinct domain concepts despite sharing the name 'Account', grounded in separate persistence (auth_db vs billing_db) and the fact that neither module imports the other directly

Identifies integration/link.py's AccountLink as the explicit translation/mapping boundary between the two, and correctly states the cardinality evidenced by its own docstring and resolve_billing_account (an auth Account has at most one linked billing Account; one with no link has never started a paid plan)
Does not claim a bounded-context split anywhere else in the repository beyond what integration/link.py's actual cross-import evidences

evals.name: canonical-vs-derived-and-lifecycle-flagging
evals.prompt: I need to work in this repository and don't know the domain yet. Get me oriented to the domain model before I touch anything. The repository is at evals/domain-orientation/cases/case-006/repo/.
evals.expected_output: Correctly identifies Product.price_cents_usd as canonical and DisplayPrice as a derived, periodically-refreshed, potentially-stale projection with no independent authority -- grounded in fx_refresh.py -- and separately flags Product.status as a lifecycle-audit candidate rather than inlining its own transition analysis.
expectations: States that Product.price_cents_usd is the canonical price and DisplayPrice is a derived/cached projection (not a peer price concept), grounded in fx_refresh.py computing DisplayPrice from price_cents_usd and never the reverse, and names that it can be stale relative to the source

Product.status is flagged as a lifecycle-audit candidate (states with transition guards in catalog/lifecycle.py) rather than the report producing its own full transition/invariant/interaction characterization of it
DisplayPrice is not described as carrying its own lifecycle or invariant of its own -- it has no transition guard, no illegal-value rule beyond being a recomputation of Product's price
